s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of immunotherapy
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine trial yielded no improvement
Biopsy showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

differentials: Annular erythema associated with Sjögren syndrome

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils

shortlist.label: Pembrolizumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and rash started after initiation of immunotherapy

shortlist.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving ipilimumab and rash started after initiation of immunotherapy

shortlist.label: Fixed drug eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Rash started after initiation of new immunotherapy regimen and did not improve with oral terbinafine

raw.rationale: Biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils, which is more consistent with eosinophilic cellulitis than erythema annulare centrifugum
raw.anchor_refutation: Erythema annulare centrifugum typically does not have significant eosinophilic infiltration on biopsy, and the clinical presentation of the rash, although annular, is more suggestive of an inflammatory process with eosinophilic involvement

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: Lack of significant eosinophilic infiltration on biopsy

rejected.label: Pembrolizumab-induced rash
rejected.why: While the patient is receiving pembrolizumab, the specific biopsy findings point more towards an eosinophilic process rather than a general drug-induced rash

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
rejected.why: Similar to pembrolizumab, the biopsy findings are more specific for an eosinophilic process than a general drug-induced rash

rejected.label: Fixed drug eruption
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not align with the typical characteristics of fixed drug eruption, which usually has a more distinct border and is often associated with a specific drug
